business_model.claim: Boston Beer makes and sells alcohol beverages: flavored malt beverages (Twisted Tea), hard seltzer (Truly), beer (Samuel Adams, Dogfish Head), hard cider (Angry Orchard), spirits RTDs (Sun Cruiser) and some distilled spirits. It brews at its own breweries and cidery and under contract at other producers' facilities.

The company sells to a network of over 300 wholesalers, who sell on to retailers such as grocery, club, convenience and liquor stores, bars and restaurants. The largest distributor was about 3% of gross sales and the top three about 7%, so distributor concentration is low.
quotes: the Company sells most of its alcohol beverages to independent beer Distributors for distribution to retailers and, ultimately, to drinkers

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A

business_model.claim: Category trends set the demand backdrop. In 2025 the flavored malt beverage category declined 4% and hard seltzer declined 4.5%, while spirits RTDs grew approximately 29%. The company's largest brands sit in the declining categories, and Sun Cruiser sits in the growing one.
quotes: Since 2021, the category has seen significant declines in volume.

quotes: In measured off-premise channels in 2025, the US Beer Market decreased 1.2% to $47.0 billion with Beyond beer increasing 4.4% to $10.7 billion and Traditional beer declining 2.8% to $36.3 billion.

growth_thesis.basis: Guidance is stated in the earnings release; the interpretation is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Guidance does not rely on volume growth: depletions and shipments are guided down mid-single digits, while the low end of non-GAAP EPS guidance rose to $9.00 from $8.50. For the guided earnings to be reached, margin, price, mix and buyback effects must carry the result in a shrinking-volume year.
quotes: Depletions and Shipments Percentage Change | Down mid-single digits | Down low-single digits to mid-single digits

material_events.basis: stated in the cited items (10-Q MD&A, balance sheet and income statement)
material_events.claim: The Company recorded a non-recurring pre-tax litigation expense of $194.5 million for the supplier dispute, made up of a judgment of $175.5 million plus pre-judgment and post-judgment interest. The balance sheet carries a matching accrued litigation liability of 194,471 (table in thousands), and the nine-month period shows an operating loss.
quotes: For the thirty-nine weeks ended September 26, 2026, the Company recorded non-recurring pre-tax litigation expense of $194.5 million, related to the supplier dispute, consisting of the judgment of $175.5 million, pre-judgment interest of $15.5 million and post-judgment interest expense of $3.5 million.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release.
